I am 68 years old, and I have been working this land in Quzhou since I was a small boy. I never went to school, but the land has been my teacher for 60 years. My wife and I are the only ones left in the household, so I must be practical. We have 11.6 mu and a well for irrigation. 

This year, I will plant **4 mu of spring maize** because it is our main food and feed, and hybrid maize still gives a reliable harvest. I will plant **3.6 mu of peanut** — the sandy loam here is good for it, and peanut brings in cash while helping the soil. I will plant **2 mu of cotton**; the price has been acceptable, but I am old now and cannot pick too much, so I keep it small. The remaining **2 mu will go to mungbean** — it grows fast, needs little care, and I can sell it in the market or cook it at home. 

I use hybrid seed for maize because everyone knows it yields more. For peanut, cotton, and mungbean, I use my own saved seed or traditional varieties from the county market — they are cheaper and I know how they behave. I fertilize by feel and memory: maize and cotton need the most nitrogen, peanut wants more phosphorus and potassium, and mungbean barely needs anything because it fixes its own nitrogen. I will rotary till the fields to control weeds and break up the soil. From the well, I will irrigate cotton three times and the others less — mungbean only once because it does not like wet feet. I will spray pesticides when I see insects, usually two or three times for cotton and maize, once for mungbean. I do not expect record yields, but after 60 years I know what this land can give me.
